evidence.requirements: Almost every point in the brief is met. The list has a Search field, a Family select and the 'n cartridges' count, and search covers alternative names (app.js:14-58, catalogue.js:20-27). The detail view has the metadata, the water capacity with its source link, the 'All cartridges' link, a Print button calling window.print, and a hash address that survives reload (detail.js, ADR 0002). Tolerances sit beside their values and angles show as 40° or D°M'S" (format.js:47-81). The drawing is computed from rules 1-9 and has dimensions for L3, L6, R, R1, P1, P2, H1, H2, G1, L1, L2, E1 and α, a title block and the accessible name. Print is one A4 page (print-308_win.jpg). Two points are only partly met. First, α is shown as a leader arrow pointing at the shoulder midpoint (layout.js:221-239), not as an angular dimension with arc and extension lines. Second, in print only the first table keeps its Symbol/Value/Unit header row (app.css:191), so the other tables have no column headers.
evidence.correctness: geometry.js follows the rules closely, and the unit tests pin each one with numbers. Checked: the chamfer (geometry.js:146-149), the groove and the belt ramp at δ (geometry.js:160-183, 300 Win. Mag. belt ramp end 3.238), the R1/P1 rim-type thresholds, the shoulder through (P2/2, L1) and (H1/2, L2) with fillets scaled to fit, the seating depth, the cylinder fraction k and the meplat per shape (BULLETS table), the tangent ogive centre, the heeled 22 LR bullet (exposed at H2, heel at H2-2tb), tn and tb, w, and the pocket sizes per primer. Outlines match the reference drawings: 308 and 300 WM proportions, the 9 mm taper and round nose, the 22 LR rounded rim and heeled bullet. Dimension values match the data, for example 'L3 51.18' and 'α 10°58'0"'. Deviations: (1) on straight cases the inner wall tapers linearly from w all the way to the bullet base (geometry.js:332), which is the agent's own interpretation and not 'tb along the body'; (2) the P1, P2, H1, H2 and G1 extension lines run horizontally along the whole part to a stack right of the bullet tip, so the P1 line nearly coincides with the body outline (detail-308_win.jpg, detail-9_3_x_74_r.jpg); (3) α has no angular dimension. Print fits one A4 page, and a test checks that for all 25 records (print.test.mjs:49-65).
evidence.security: There is one innerHTML (drawing.js:186), and it receives an SVG string where every record string is escaped by esc() (drawing.js:22-24) and all numbers are formatted. The rest of the DOM is built with createElement and text nodes (dom.js). There is no eval, no fetch, no CDN and no fonts, and e2e tests assert that no foreign requests are made. The dev server checks paths with startsWith(ROOT) and has no trailing-separator check; it is dev-only and binds to 127.0.0.1.
evidence.code_quality: The code splits cleanly into pure geometry, layout, drawing and view modules with UMD wrappers so Node tests can require them (ADR 0001). Names are clear and constants are named (BULLETS, PRIMERS, FONT_MIN). A failed label placement is caught and turned into a drawing note instead of a crash (drawing.js:157-166). layout.js is dense: there are several magic em factors, and the label placement search is fairly involved. Size is reasonable for the task, about 1,100 lines of JS.
evidence.tests: The tests are thorough. Unit tests check each geometry rule against hand-computed points: chamfer, groove, belt, rimfire half-round, fillets, ogive and ellipse sampling, heeled bullet, walls, w, pocket, and missing-value notes. Layout tests check the full set of dimension IDs, label texts, and that no label touches another label, the outline or other lines for all 25 records. E2e tests run over file:// and http: list, search and filter, metadata, every value row and tolerance, focus, malformed hashes, rendered-label overlap in Chromium, phone width, dark mode, print colours, a one-page PDF for all 25 records, and label size on paper.
evidence.ux_design: The tables are dense and calm: grouped by section, tabular numbers, values right-aligned, tolerances muted beside the value. The drawing is clean and has no label overlaps. On desktop, though, the part takes about half the panel width, the monospace labels are large relative to it, and the title block is oversized, leaving a large empty area at the bottom left (detail-308_win.jpg, detail-44_rem_mag.jpg). Long blue extension lines run across the body and bullet, so the outline is harder to read than the reference, where dimensions sit at the feature. Primer types show as raw codes ('lr', 'sp'). The print layout is tight and professional: a 5-column meta strip, a full-width drawing, 4-column tables and a footer (print-308_win.jpg).
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img, aria-label '<name> drawing', a <title>, and a <desc> that includes the notes (drawing.js:86-92). Tables have captions and th scope. Inputs have labels, the count has role=status, focus moves to the h1 on navigation, and :focus-visible outlines are set. Bug: the skip link uses href="#main" (index.html:12). With hash routing, activating it fires hashchange, and route() renders the list (app.js:66-70), so on a detail page 'Skip to content' throws the user back to the list. Uppercase labels at 0.7-0.74rem in muted grey are small.
evidence.simplicity: Plain HTML, CSS and JS. The only dev dependency is Playwright, and there are no runtime dependencies or build step. The amount of code fits the problem. The label-placement engine is the heaviest part, and it is justified by the no-overlap requirement.
evidence.maintainability: README covers use, files, how it was built and tests. There are two ADRs and a GLOSSARY. The lockfile pins Playwright, and the test suite is a strong regression net. Missing: any CI configuration, a Node version pin (no engines field and no .nvmrc, although the brief says Node 22), and a changelog or release notes beyond version 1.0.0. README also points to `.scratch/cartridge-reference/` for the spec, which is not in the repository.
evidence.visual_design: Restrained, consistent typography. System sans is used for the UI and monospace for symbols and drawing labels, and the light palette is calm with one blue accent. The table cards are evenly aligned across pages. The drawing's blue labels look heavy next to the thin part outline, and the big black title block is visually out of proportion. Dark mode is defined in CSS but not visible in the screenshots.
evidence.layout: The hierarchy is clear: back link and Print, then the name, the meta grid, the drawing, and the tables in cartridge and chamber groups (all detail screenshots). There is no clipping or overflow. Inside the drawing panel, space is used poorly: the part is small, there is empty whitespace left of the title block, and the dimension stack sits far right of the tip. The print page leaves about a quarter of A4 empty at the bottom while the drawing could be larger.
evidence.usability: Tasks take few steps. Search works on alternative names and decimal-comma variants, the family filter combines with search, name links go to bookmarkable hash URLs, filter state survives going back to the list, and unknown addresses get a 'Not found' page with a link back. Print is one click. Two small issues: the skip-link bug, and primer and family values are unexplained codes.
evidence.reception: Reloaders and engineers would trust it: values exactly as published, tolerances in place, C.I.P. table and revision in the title block, a clean one-page printout, and a true-to-scale computed drawing with a hatched section. The oversized labels and title block, the extension lines crossing the part, and α shown without a real angular dimension make the drawing look less like a proper engineering drawing than the reference does.

unmet_requirements: Shoulder angle α is labelled with a leader arrow to the shoulder midpoint, not as an angular dimension line with arrowheads and extension lines (layout.js:221-239).
In print, every value table except the first hides its Symbol/Value/Unit header row (app.css:191).
Section walls on straight cases taper linearly from the head to the bullet base instead of staying at tb along the body (geometry.js:332); this is the agent's own interpretation of rule 8.
strengths: The drawing geometry implements rules 1-9 faithfully: chamfer, groove, belt at δ, rimfire half-round, filleted shoulder, ogive, ellipse and cone noses, the heeled 22 LR, walls, head and pocket. Outlines and proportions match the reference drawings.
The test suite is excellent: unit tests pin each rule numerically, and browser tests check rendered-label overlaps, all value rows, and a one-page A4 PDF for all 25 records.
Values, tolerances, angles and units are shown exactly as the brief asks. The print view is a clean one-page A4 sheet with header, full-width drawing, dense tables and source footer.
issues: Drawing legibility on screen: the part takes only about half the panel, labels and the title block are oversized, and the P1/P2/H1/H2/G1 extension lines run across the whole body and bullet to a stack right of the tip, nearly overlapping the outline. α has only a leader, not an angular dimension.
The skip link (href="#main") triggers the hash router and renders the list, so on a detail page 'Skip to content' throws the user back to the list (index.html:12, app.js:66-70).

Maintainability gaps: no CI pipeline, no pinned Node version, no release notes, and the README points to a spec folder that is not in the repository. Only the first table keeps its column headers in print.
review.verdict: This is a careful, well-tested build: the drawing follows the brief's geometry rules almost exactly, the data is shown precisely, and the printout is a clean one-page A4 sheet. Before publishing, the on-screen drawing composition (label size, extension lines along the outline, α dimension) and the skip-link routing bug should be fixed, and CI and a Node version pin should be added.
